# User stories

MechaHarness acceptance paths are told as **user stories**: short scenes about what a product needs to do, written for readers who understand features but not code. Each story has a human **narrative**, an **implementation** section that traces library code fulfilling the feature, and a **validation** section that describes how the story is tested. Story text lives only in fixture `story.json` files. This guide is **generated** from those fixtures.

See the Cursor skill `.cursor/skills/user-stories/SKILL.md` when adding features: edit fixtures, regenerate this page, and keep twin copies of the same story id identical.

## Personas

### Nubble — operations / DevOps

Nubble keeps production and CI reliable. He cares about the right inference profile being loaded, cost and progress signals he can forward to billing or monitoring, and metrics that explain whether parallel work actually helped.

### Fangore — application developer

Fangore builds product applications on MechaHarness. He cares about deny-by-default permissions, product rules that models cannot override, durable local plans that survive crashes, loops that stop when they are not making progress, and context that never silently drops mandatory requirements.

### Taloneth — ML engineer

Taloneth owns judge contracts, adapter drift checks, and harness experiments. He cares about offline fixture batches, versioned recorded replies, honest shadow comparisons, validator qualification before promotion, research that rejects failing candidates, and decision exports that do not leak future outcomes.

## Running the suite

Default CI runs **every** story offline (static fixture + cassettes) — no skips.

```bash
# CI / offline — all stories, zero skips
pytest -q tests/stories

# Full suite (unit + stories)
pytest -q

# Live OpenAI-compat — same tests, real HTTP
MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live MECHA_STORY_MODEL=openai_compat/qwen3-30b-thinking \
  MECHA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 pytest -q tests/stories -k nubble_run_cost

# Live System One
MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live MECHA_STORY_MODEL=systemone/laya \
  MECHA_JUDGE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8009 pytest -q tests/stories -k refund_verdict

# Shorthand aliases (still dual-mode stories, not separate skipif modules)
MECHA_LIVE_OPENAI_COMPAT=1 MECHA_BASE_URL=… pytest -q tests/stories -k nubble_run_cost
MECHA_LIVE_QWEN=1 MECHA_BASE_URL=… pytest -q tests/stories -k nubble_run_cost
MECHA_LIVE_JUDGE=1 pytest -q tests/stories -k 'refund_verdict or systemone_cassette'
```

| `MECHA_STORY_BACKEND` | Behavior |
|-----------------------|----------|
| `static` (default) | In-process fixture + HTTP cassettes |
| `live` | Real servers; soft expects only |

Live parity is a **mode** of cassette-backed stories (for example `nubble_run_cost_events`, `fangore_refund_verdict`, `taloneth_systemone_cassette`), not a separate empty fixture. Flip `MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live` to run the same request and expect files against a real endpoint.

| Path | Role |

## Nubble's stories

### `nubble_ci_static_smoke` — Prove the HTTP adapter in CI without a live model host

The local inference host is offline, but a pull request still needs green CI. Nubble wants the OpenAI-compatible path proven from a cassette — a recorded reply replayed through the real HTTP client — so merges do not depend on LAN reachability.

#### Implementation

`OpenAICompatStrategy` implements Chat Completions HTTP for reason-lane backends. Cassette replay exercises the real client path so adapter wire shape stays honest in CI.

Covers: offline CI / OpenAI-compat smoke.

#### Validation

Kind `pass_through` on `openai_compat` trees with mock transport. Soft expects: non-empty assistant text. Live: `MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live`.

#### Footnotes

1. [OpenAI Chat Completions](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat) — Wire models for reason-lane HTTP

### `nubble_lane_load_hint` — Refuse work when the wrong inference profile is loaded

Nubble is on call when a refund-routing job fails on the local inference host. The job needs the judge profile, but an earlier experiment left the reason profile loaded instead. The harness must not fail with a vague error. It must tell him, in plain operator language, that this work needs the judge lane and which load command to run. When he switches to the correct profile, the page clears. He uses this story whenever a profile mismatch wastes incident time.

#### Implementation

Exclusive lanes (reason / decide-judge / media) on `InferenceEnvironment` refuse cross-lane work and surface load hints (`DEFAULT_LANE_LOAD_HINTS`). This is the operator-facing half of decide-versus-reason profile discipline: bounded judge work must not run under a generative reason profile. Hosts supply a real environment via Config instead of `NoOpInferenceEnvironment`.

Covers: INF-02.

#### Validation

Kind `wrong_lane_deny` → `_run_wrong_lane_deny`. Soft expects: non-empty error naming the required lane / load hint. Unit: `tests/test_environment.py`.

### `nubble_model_affinity` — Keep model affinity inside a coherent work loop

Within one coherent loop, Nubble wants routing to prefer the already-chosen lane unless a phase boundary justifies a switch. Random lane thrash must not win on unit price alone.

#### Implementation

`route_at_boundary` selects lanes at task/phase boundaries; `activate_scoped_policy` activates judgement policy only when calibration criteria are met — affinity and activation stay behind evaluation, not cheapest unit price.

Covers: RTE-03.

#### Validation

Kind `model_affinity` → `_run_model_affinity`. Soft expects: preferred lane selected for task kind; uncalibrated policy activation returns null. Unit: `tests/test_routing.py`.

### `nubble_repo_topology` — Budget repository topology maps and fall back when stale

Nubble feeds the context compiler a budgeted repository map. When the map is over budget or stale, the system must omit paths honestly and still allow source inspection fallback — not pretend the map is complete.

#### Implementation

`RepositoryTopologyProvider` builds budgeted `TopologyView` entries with omissions and invalidation; stale maps fall back to source inspection.

Covers: CTX-08.

#### Validation

Kind `repo_topology` → `_run_repo_topology`. Unit: `tests/test_context_experiments.py`.

### `nubble_run_cost_events` — Record cost and inference events for every harness run

Finance asks Nubble whether a harness run actually burned billable units. He runs a short one-shot job and checks the event log. He needs both an inference event and a cost event with non-zero units — the same signals he would forward to billing or a Grafana panel.

#### Implementation

Harness runs emit structured `EventLog` records for inference and cost (`CostAccountant` / `core:cost`, `core:inference`). This is the baseline observability stream for every run — decisions, routing, and tools extend the same log rather than a separate ledger.

Covers: OBS-01.

#### Validation

Kind `pass_through` → `_run_pass_through`. Soft expects: inference and cost events with non-zero units. Related: `tests/test_events.py`, `tests/test_pass_through.py`.

### `nubble_topology_efficiency` — Separate wall-clock speedup from total work and queue wait

Nubble is asked whether parallel agents sped things up. Wall time dropped, but total work grew and queue waits hid under a vanity speedup. He needs metrics that separate critical path, total work, and elapsed time — and that refuse misleading efficiency claims without a serial baseline and worker-count note.

#### Implementation

`compute_topology_metrics` / `TopologySpan` in `mechaharness.decision_log` report critical path, total work, and elapsed time distinctly and reject vanity speedups that omit baselines.

Covers: OBS-04.

#### Validation

Kind `topology_efficiency` → `_run_topology_efficiency`. Unit: `tests/test_decision_log.py`.

## Fangore's stories

### `fangore_bounded_repair_loop` — Bound verification repair loops to a fixed number of attempts

After a failed verification, Fangore allows a limited repair-and-retry cycle. When attempts are exhausted, the node stays failed — it does not loop forever. Complements `fangore_convergence_ceiling` for judge loops and `fangore_verification_outcome_gate` for completion versus answer-generated. See inspiration requirements for verification loops[^insp-repair].

#### Implementation

`bounded_repair` in `mechaharness.graph` runs verify → classify → permitted repair → retry until `max_attempts`. `VerificationPolicy` / `OutcomeContract` select verification and gate completion. Judge scores remain supplementary to verifier evidence.

Covers: VER-03.

#### Validation

Kind `bounded_repair_loop` → `_run_bounded_repair_loop`. Soft expects: succeeds within budget or fails after max attempts. Unit: `tests/test_graph.py`. Related: `fangore_verification_outcome_gate`.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-repair]: [Inspiration requirements (verification loops)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 5 — verification is part of execution; structured enough to route repair

### `fangore_capability_envelope_narrow` — Narrow child capability envelopes without silent inheritance

Fangore delegates a child plan with fewer tools and grants than the parent. The child must not quietly inherit the parent's full capability set, and attempts to widen grants beyond the parent must fail closed. See inspiration requirements for delegation envelopes[^insp-envelope].

#### Implementation

`CapabilityEnvelope` in `mechaharness.capability_envelope` carries grants, tools, context provider ids, model class, budgets, and escalation policy. `narrow()` produces a child envelope that cannot widen parent grants or tools. Attached on `GraphRunContext.envelope` during graph runs. `DefaultDelegationPolicy` chooses inline versus child/subgraph using independence and pollution signals.

#### Validation

Kind `capability_envelope_narrow` → `_run_capability_envelope_narrow`. Soft expects: narrowed grants subset; widen raises; delegation chooses child when independence is required. Unit: `tests/test_inspiration_primitives.py`.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-envelope]: [Inspiration requirements (delegation envelopes)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 7 — CapabilityEnvelope; children must not inherit parent capabilities implicitly

### `fangore_completer_flavors` — Wire same-lane Completer flavors without forking the library

Fangore’s product needs a deep code Completer beside the default reason Completer in one Config. He registers a second Named flavor and a small host harness that selects it with Annotated Matched tags — no marker-lane ABCs and no edits to MechaHarness enums.

#### Implementation

`MechaHarnessConfig.completer_bindings()` registers `Named` Completer tag sets (lane + host flavors). Host constructors declare `Annotated[Completer, Named(...)]` / `Matched(...)`. Bare `inject(Completer)` keeps the default aliased to `InferenceStrategy`. Lanes on `InferenceEnvironment` stay capability partitions; flavors are DI bindings.

Covers: same-lane Completer flavors via pyiv Named/Matched.

#### Validation

Kind `completer_flavors` → `_run_completer_flavors`. Unit: `tests/test_di.py`.

#### Footnotes

1. [pyiv Named/Matched](https://rl337.org/pyiv/) — Named / Matched / Annotated constructor injection

### `fangore_compound_grants` — Compose read-only and write permission packs

Fangore’s host app must not let agents write the filesystem by default. A read-only pack refuses the write tool; composing it with a write pack allows the same tool. He needs reusable permission packs instead of copy-pasted lists.

#### Implementation

`AccessPolicy` deny-by-default grants; `CompoundPolicy` unions packs; `AccessControl` enforces tool grants and emits access-check events. This is the permission half of tool gating — every tool call must pass access before side effects.

Covers: host compound grants.

#### Validation

Kind `grant_gate_write` → `_run_grant_gate_write`. Unit: `tests/test_access.py`.

### `fangore_config_access_policy` — Let the host app supply its own permission policy

Fangore’s product needs permission rules defined by the application. He configures the harness once so composed packs from `fangore_compound_grants` are what the harness enforces.

#### Implementation

`MechaHarnessConfig` hooks (`get_access_policy`, `get_access_control`, `get_grants`) bind host permission packs through pyiv injection — not Settings bags or hand-wired harness constructors. Fangore subclasses Config once; the injector builds `AccessControl` and the harness with those grants.

Covers: host DI access policy.

#### Validation

Kind `config_access_policy` → `_run_config_access_policy`. Unit: `tests/test_di.py`.

#### Footnotes

1. [pyiv](https://rl337.org/pyiv/) — Config-hook dependency injection

### `fangore_consequence_risk_scale` — Scale autonomy controls by action consequence

Fangore marks a destructive write as high consequence. Low-risk reads may proceed under ordinary grants; high-consequence actions must trigger stronger controls and track how often humans are prompted so approval fatigue stays visible. Soft prompts alone must not replace hard grants. See inspiration requirements for risk-scaled autonomy[^insp-risk].

#### Implementation

`ConsequencePolicy` / `ActionConsequence` in `mechaharness.consequence` classify actions (`low`…`critical`), flag approval and exhaustive verification needs, and expose `approval_frequency` as a usability/safety metric. Grants in `AccessControl` remain the hard gate.

#### Validation

Kind `consequence_risk_scale` → `_run_consequence_risk_scale`. Soft expects: high-consequence write requires stronger controls; approval frequency recorded. Unit: `tests/test_inspiration_primitives.py`. Related grants: `fangore_tool_gating`.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-risk]: [Inspiration requirements (risk-scaled autonomy)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Reqs 9 and 15 — soft vs hard mechanisms; consequence-scaled autonomy

Mandatory blockers must not disappear when the prompt budget is tight. Success is a deficit report with unresolved gaps named. Related observation chain: `fangore_context_observation_chain`.

#### Implementation

`ContextCompiler` builds a versioned `ContextManifest` with token estimates and unresolved gaps. Working context is ephemeral; obligations stay in authoritative stores.

Kind `context_compiler_deficit` → `_run_context_compiler_deficit`. Unit: `tests/test_context_experiments.py`.

### `fangore_context_observation_chain` — Keep original observations and refuse fabricated reductions

Tool output must stay addressable as an immutable observation. A cheaper summary is allowed only when it points at a real observation; fabricated receipts must fail lookup. Compaction happens at semantic boundaries, and action fusion only for predeclared sequences. Compiler deficits remain `fangore_context_compiler_deficit`.

#### Implementation

`ObservationStore` / `ObservationRef`, `reduce_evidence`, `compact_at_boundary`, and `fuse_actions` under `CtxFlags` in `mechaharness.context_experiments`.

Covers: CTX-01, CTX-02, CTX-03, CTX-04.

#### Validation

### `fangore_convergence_ceiling` — Stop agent loops that make no progress

Fangore’s repair loop keeps asking the same question and getting the same answer. A versioned ceiling must end as no-progress — never fake success — and nested repair must share parent budget. Graph repeating nodes additionally require an explicit stop contract at linkage (`fangore_graph_linkage_preflight`). See inspiration requirements for stop contracts[^insp-stop].

#### Implementation

`ConvergenceContract` / `ConvergenceGuard` fingerprint windows and nested budget slices. `StopContract` in `mechaharness.stop_contract` is the graph-facing alias for the same ceilings plus trigger/continuation/success/abort fields. Escalation may request more evidence, but ceilings never count as task success.

Covers: POL-03.

#### Validation

Kind `convergence_ceiling` → `_run_convergence_ceiling`. Unit: `tests/test_convergence.py`. Linkage stop enforcement: `fangore_graph_linkage_preflight`.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-stop]: [Inspiration requirements (stop contracts)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 4 — repeating execution requires an explicit stop contract

### `fangore_decision_surface_reject` — Reject model choices that are not on the allowed list

A triage model returns a team name that was never on the allowed set. The product must treat that as a rejected proposal. Only product judgement policy may unlock the next action — same split as `fangore_refund_verdict`.

#### Implementation

`DecisionSurface` / `reject_invalid_choice` / `RulesDecisionBackend` in `mechaharness.decision_surfaces` name the decision plane over judge signal types. Surfaces produce signals; they do not execute side effects.

#### Validation

Kind `decision_surface_reject` → `_run_decision_surface_reject`.

### `fangore_derived_memory` — Rebuild derived memory without letting rank invent authority

When derived memory is enabled, Fangore needs idempotent consolidation, rebuild from events, and a hard rule: high retrieval rank must not confer authority over approval rules.

`DerivedMemoryStore` / `DerivedMemoryRecord` separate provenance, validity, and retrieval priority. Consolidation is optional and idempotent; `retrieval_candidates` must not elevate non-authoritative rumors.

### `fangore_graph_executor` — Run a local plan through an authorized graph executor

Fangore ships a host app with a produce → repair → consume plan. After linkage succeeds, the library must walk ready steps, refuse execution without an execute grant, retry transient failures, escalate when retries are exhausted, emit start and end telemetry, and finish the downstream consume step only after upstream success. Checkpointed plans from `fangore_local_plan_resume` stay durable; preflight failures are covered by `fangore_graph_linkage_preflight`. See inspiration requirements for authorized graph execution[^insp-executor].

#### Implementation

`GraphExecutor` in `mechaharness.graph_executor` is a pyiv injectable: constructor takes `EventLog`, `AccessControl`, `GraphNodeRunnerRegistry`, `GraphFailurePolicy`, `GraphEscalation`, and `LinkageResolver`. Hosts register node runners by open `kind` string via `MechaHarnessConfig.get_node_runner_registry()`, override failure/escalation/linkage hooks, and grant `core:graph.execute` / `core:graph.escalate`. The executor emits `core:graph_start` / `core:graph_end` plus per-node events, checkpoints through `GraphStore` (with config fingerprint), and enforces per-runner grants.

#### Validation

Kind `graph_executor_run` → `_run_graph_executor_run`. Soft expects: denied without execute grant; ok status with consume sum; graph_start/graph_end present; flaky attempts before escalation. Static matrix: `tests/fixtures/graph_executor/*.json` via `tests/test_graph_executor.py`. Related: `fangore_graph_linkage_preflight`.

#### Footnotes

[^loop-vs-graph-executor]: [Loop vs graph engineering](https://medium.com/@neuraldev/loop-engineering-vs-graph-engineering-the-architecture-shift-quietly-reshaping-ai-agents-c83488435d23) — Executor advances durable plans hosts define
[^insp-executor]: [Inspiration requirements (graph execution)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Reqs 2 and 12 — linkage then execute; durable checkpoints

### `fangore_graph_linkage_preflight` — Fail closed on missing graph linkage before work starts

Fangore composes a plan that still names a step the host has not wired, and another repeating step without a stop rule. The library must refuse those plans before any runner work starts, naming the missing edge so operators can fix wiring instead of debugging a mid-run crash. Complements `fangore_graph_executor` (authorized run once linkage is sound) and `fangore_convergence_ceiling` (budgets once a loop is allowed). See the inspiration requirements for linkage versus dependency injection and stop contracts[^insp-linkage].

#### Implementation

`DefaultLinkageResolver` in `mechaharness.linkage_resolver` validates runner kinds, grants, environment compatibility, termination sinks, and repeating nodes' `StopContract` before `GraphExecutor` substantive work. Missing runners and missing stop contracts become structured `UnsatisfiedEdge` codes (`no_runner`, `missing_stop_contract`). `GraphExecutor.run` records linkage failure without invoking node handlers.

#### Validation

Kind `graph_linkage_preflight` → `_run_graph_linkage_preflight`. Soft expects: missing-runner linkage fails with `no_runner`; repeating node without stop fails with `missing_stop_contract`; valid linear graph reports `ok` with a fingerprint. Unit: `tests/test_linkage_resolver.py`, fixtures under `tests/fixtures/linkage_resolver/`.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-linkage]: [Inspiration requirements (linkage & stop contracts)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Reqs 2 and 4 — primitive DI vs runtime graph resolution; explicit stop contracts

### `fangore_graph_template_soft_points` — Instantiate a reusable graph template with soft points

Fangore picks a library fan-out template, fills only the soft points the host owns (branch payloads, runner kind names, acceptance), and keeps the resulting concrete plan in the host app. The skeleton must stamp which template produced it so later upgrades can detect drift. Independent-review and verify-repair templates follow the same pattern. See inspiration requirements for dynamic subgraphs and template incubation[^insp-templates].

#### Implementation

`mechaharness.graph_templates` ships parameterized skeletons (`FanOutAggregateTemplate`, `VerifyRepairTemplate`, `IndependentReviewTemplate`, `EnvironmentRepairTemplate`) with declared `SoftPoint`s. `GraphTemplate.instantiate` builds via `build` then stamps `template_name`, `template_version`, `template_status`, and optional `source_workflow_ref`. Demoted templates refuse instantiate. Bound via `MechaHarnessConfig.get_graph_template_registry()`.

#### Validation

### `fangore_human_review_pending` — Hold mutations until a matching human approval exists

Fangore’s product allows an agent to propose a privileged write, but the write must not run until a human approval matches the action digest. Without that token, policy returns ask-human — not allow.

#### Implementation

`JudgementPolicy.require_approval_for` plus `JudgementFacts.approvals` / `action_digest` in `decide()`: missing approval yields `ASK_HUMAN` with `MISSING_APPROVAL`. Approvals bind to executed args via digest keys.

Covers: POL-04, GAT-04.

#### Validation

Kind `human_review_pending` → `_run_human_review_pending`. Soft expects: ASK_HUMAN without token; ALLOW when digest approval present. Unit coverage in `tests/test_judgement_policy.py`.

When a parent step embeds a child graph, child node costs must count against the same budget the parent is running under. `GraphExecutor` passes the parent `Budget` into nested `run` for subgraph nodes so charges aggregate. Soft breach after the child cancels remaining parent work (`soft_exhausted`).

### `fangore_insp_graph_budget` — Enforce soft and hard spend limits on graph runs

Every graph run must declare how much spend is allowed. Crossing the soft limit winds remaining steps down without treating the job as a hard failure. Crossing the hard limit stops the run immediately. Hard can also be unlimited when no ceiling applies. Related: `fangore_insp_budget_subgraph_rollup` for nested spend, and `fangore_insp_stop_contract` for repeating-step ceilings.[^insp-budget]

#### Implementation

`BudgetPolicy` / `Budget` in `mechaharness.budget`. `GraphExecutor.run` requires `budget_policy`; each node attempt charges the shared ledger. Soft cancel open nodes → status `soft_exhausted`; hard fail open nodes → `hard_budget_exceeded`. `hard_limit=None` means unlimited.

#### Validation

Kind `graph_budget_limits`. Soft expects soft wind-down then hard fail levels. Related fixtures: `tests/fixtures/graph_executor/budget_*.json`, `tests/test_budget.py`.

### `fangore_insp_lifecycle_block` — Skip one tool call without inventing a new plan

Before a dangerous tool runs, Fangore's extension blocks that single call. The default tool does not run; the agent receives a structured skip for that step. Blocking one call does not insert a new step in a durable plan graph and does not bypass host hard-deny rules for other calls. Complements `fangore_insp_lifecycle_observe` and `fangore_insp_soft_vs_hard`. Accepts inspiration requirement 20.

#### Implementation

`LifecycleExtension` with block mode returns block at `BeforeTool`; `AbstractHarness.execute_tools` skips tool execution and emits an error tool result plus `core:extension_applied` with default_ran false.

#### Validation

Kind `lifecycle_extension_block`. Soft expects blocked tool content, applied_block true, and default_ran false.

#### Footnotes

1. [Inspiration requirements (req 20: block mode)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 20 — block

### `fangore_insp_lifecycle_graph_observe` — Watch graph node attempts without replacing failure policy

Fangore binds an observe-only extension around each graph node attempt. The node still runs through the normal runner and failure policy. The log records the extension at the graph-node boundary. This does not invent a second plan graph. Complements `fangore_insp_lifecycle_observe`. Accepts inspiration requirement 20.

#### Implementation

`GraphExecutor._run_node` dispatches observe-only lifecycle extensions at `BeforeGraphNode` / `AfterGraphNode` while `GraphFailurePolicy` remains the sole retry brain.

#### Validation

Kind `lifecycle_extension_graph_observe`. Soft expects a before_graph_node extension event and a successful graph run.

#### Footnotes

1. [Inspiration requirements (req 20: graph observe)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 20 — graph observe

### `fangore_insp_lifecycle_observe` — Watch tool calls in a fixed order without changing them

Fangore binds two host extensions that watch each tool call before it runs. The first always runs before the second. The tool still executes with the original arguments. The run log records both extensions, their order, and that the default tool action still ran. Accepts inspiration requirement 20[^insp-r20]. Complements `fangore_insp_soft_vs_hard`: watching is not permission.

#### Implementation

`LifecycleExtensionRegistry` (Config hook `get_lifecycle_extension_registry`) dispatches ordered observe extensions at `BeforeTool` / `AfterTool` inside `AbstractHarness.execute_tools`, emitting `core:extension_applied` provenance. Mutative modes are not required for this story.

#### Validation

Kind `lifecycle_extension_observe`. Soft expects two extension ids in order, default_ran true, and the original tool path in the tool result.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-r20]: [Inspiration requirements (req 20: lifecycle interception)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 20 — lifecycle interception

For one tool boundary, Fangore may substitute a different single-step outcome instead of running the original tool. That substitution is not a hidden extra node in the execution graph; multi-step repair or fan-out still uses an explicit plan. Complements `fangore_insp_lifecycle_rewrite`. Accepts inspiration requirement 20.

#### Implementation

`LifecycleExtension` with replace mode returns `replace_content` at `BeforeTool`; the harness emits that content as the tool result without executing the tool and without adding graph nodes.

#### Validation

Kind `lifecycle_extension_replace`. Soft expects replaced content, applied_replace true, and default_ran false.

1. [Inspiration requirements (req 20: replace mode)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 20 — replace

### `fangore_insp_lifecycle_rewrite` — Change tool arguments without changing the workflow

Before a write tool runs, Fangore's extension rewrites the path argument into a sandbox directory. The same write tool still runs — only the arguments change. Hard grants still apply to the rewritten call; the extension cannot widen permission by rewriting to a more privileged tool. The log shows that a rewrite ran and that the default tool still ran. Accepts inspiration requirement 20. Complements `fangore_insp_lifecycle_observe`.

#### Implementation

`LifecycleExtension` with rewrite mode returns modified arguments at `BeforeTool`; `AbstractHarness.execute_tools` runs the same tool with rewritten args, then AccessControl still gates the call.

#### Validation

Kind `lifecycle_extension_rewrite`. Soft expects sandbox path in the tool result, applied_rewrite true, and default_ran true.

#### Footnotes

1. [Inspiration requirements (req 20: rewrite mode)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 20 — rewrite

Reusable templates expose soft points and stamp provenance onto concrete graphs. Demoted templates that proved application-specific refuse instantiate. Accepts inspiration requirement 19[^insp-r19].

Producing an answer is not the same as finishing the task when verification is required. Accepts inspiration requirement 5[^insp-r05].

Persistent goals live in the client orchestrator. When a goal wakes, MechaHarness must re-resolve linkage and resume only if the checkpoint fingerprint still matches. Accepts the library half of inspiration requirement 17[^insp-r17].

#### Implementation

Client wakes call `LinkageResolver` then `GraphExecutor.run(resume=True)`. Fingerprint mismatch fails closed. Goal stores remain outside the library.

Fangore limits concurrent active nodes and per-write-scope work so agents cannot overreach, while hosts still choose thresholds rather than a universal WIP=1. Accepts WalkingLabs L07 and L08 guidance[^wl-l07-wip][^wl-l08-wip].

#### Implementation

`WorkInProgressPolicy` in `mechaharness.work_in_progress_policy` gates concurrency by active nodes, write scope, resource class, and consequence.

#### Validation

Kind `wip_policy_allows`. Soft expects allow then deny when scope saturated.

[^wl-l07-wip]: [WalkingLabs L07 Task Boundaries](https://walkinglabs.github.io/learn-harness-engineering/en/lectures/lecture-07-why-agents-overreach-and-under-finish/) — Bound WIP
[^wl-l08-wip]: [WalkingLabs L08 Feature Lists](https://walkinglabs.github.io/learn-harness-engineering/en/lectures/lecture-08-why-feature-lists-are-harness-primitives/) — Back-pressure

### `fangore_local_plan_resume` — Resume a durable local plan after a crash

A local plan fans out produce-then-consume work. The process dies mid-dispatch. On restart, checkpoints — not chat — must resume at the recorded boundary, keep justified edges, refuse stale preconditions, surface failed fan-in, and refuse silent overwrite on conflicting writes. Incompatible harness or graph fingerprints must refuse silent continue. See inspiration requirements for durable long-running work[^insp-resume].

#### Implementation

`OperationContract` / `OperationRegistry` register shared computation contracts with scopes, preconditions, and effect classes, plus a capability registry of revisions. `ExecutionGraph` / `GraphStore` persist goal, nodes, and justified dependency edges on `EventLog` with recovery boundaries and optional `config_fingerprint`; effect isolation, hierarchical fan-in, and merge conflict policy cover parallel writes. Global loop stays under convergence; the DAG is local.

Covers: INF-01, INF-03, GRF-01, GRF-02, GRF-03, GRF-04, GRF-05, GRF-06.

#### Validation

Kind `local_plan_resume` → `_run_local_plan_resume`. Unit: `tests/test_graph.py`, `tests/test_operation_registry.py`. Fingerprint refuse covered in `tests/test_inspiration_primitives.py`.

#### Footnotes

[^loop-vs-graph]: [Loop vs graph engineering](https://medium.com/@neuraldev/loop-engineering-vs-graph-engineering-the-architecture-shift-quietly-reshaping-ai-agents-c83488435d23) — Explicit control flow; MechaHarness extends into execution graphs
[^insp-resume]: [Inspiration requirements (durable resume)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 12 — resumable external state; incompatible fingerprint refuse

### `fangore_refund_verdict` — Keep billing authority in product rules, not the model

A customer was charged twice. Only the billing team may own the ticket. The model may suggest a team, but product policy allows only when the route signal is billing — and a high quality score alone must not override missing completion evidence. See also `fangore_decision_surface_reject`.

#### Implementation

Provider-neutral judge types (`Choice`/`Score`/`Noul` questions and signals) plus `JudgementPolicy` / `decide()` apply configured thresholds. Judge scores are supplementary: policy owns ALLOW/DENY. Thresholds live in policy config per signal id. System One maps vendor wire into these types via `SystemOneJudgeProvider`.

Covers: POL-02, JDG-01, JDG-02, JDG-04, VER-02.

#### Validation

Kind `route_refund` → `_run_route_refund`. Soft expects: ALLOW for billing, DENY for technical. Unit: `tests/test_judgement_policy.py`, `tests/test_judge.py`.

#### Footnotes

1. [Jev decisions in a Pi harness](https://academy.dair.ai/resources/jev-decisions-in-a-pi-sdk-harness) — Routing, gating, batched questions, thresholds

### `fangore_sparse_advisor_consult` — Consult an advisor sparsely without transferring ownership

Fangore's worker hits a consequential planning boundary and asks a stronger advisor for counsel. The worker keeps ownership of the task: advice is guidance, not a hand-off, and a budget must stop low-value routine consultation. See inspiration requirements for the advisor pattern[^insp-advisor].

#### Implementation

`Advisor` / `AdvisorPolicy` in `mechaharness.advisor` are distinct from `GraphEscalation` (ownership transfer). `DefaultAdvisorPolicy` rate-limits consultations; `consult_advisor` records `AdvisorObservation` and never transfers task ownership. Default DI binds `RejectAdvisor` with an explicit continue fallback.

#### Validation

Kind `sparse_advisor_consult` → `_run_sparse_advisor_consult`. Soft expects: first consultation returns guidance; second blocked by budget; observation recorded. Unit: `tests/test_inspiration_primitives.py`.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-advisor]: [Inspiration requirements (advisor)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 18 — sparse non-binding advisor; executor retains ownership

### `fangore_tool_gating` — Gate every tool call through deny-by-default access checks

Every tool call — including fused or loop-proposed calls — must pass access control. Uncertain or privileged scopes fail closed. Soft prompt guidance never replaces these hard grants. Fangore shows product that a write without grant is refused and that composed packs from `fangore_compound_grants` still apply. See inspiration requirements for soft versus hard enforcement[^insp-soft-hard].

#### Implementation

Harness tool loops consult `AccessControl` before execution; denied calls emit access-check events and do not run side effects. Failure defaults are deny for mutations / external / privileged / uncertain scope. This story covers tool-gating obligations alongside permission packs.

Covers: GAT-01, GAT-02, GAT-03.

#### Validation

Kind `tool_gating` → `_run_tool_gating`. Soft expects: deny without grant, allow with grant. Related: `tests/test_access.py`, grant_gate story, `fangore_consequence_risk_scale`.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-soft-hard]: [Inspiration requirements (soft vs hard)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 9 — soft guidance and hard enforcement are different mechanisms

### `fangore_transactional_durable_resume` — Resume a coding job after process crash without duplicate dispatch

Fangore's host dispatches a long-running coding job through a durable plan. The MechaHarness process can die after the remote system accepts the job but before the plan records the result. On restart, the same durable store must reconcile the existing job instead of starting a second one. Crash points before intent, after intent, after accept, after reduce, and after final commit are all covered. Complements `fangore_insp_durable_resume` fingerprint refusal. Accepts the transactional durable resume requirements[^tdr-req].

#### Implementation

`GraphExecutor` injects `CheckpointStore` via `MechaHarnessConfig.get_checkpoint_store()` (SQLite reference: `SqliteCheckpointStore`; default EventLog adapter is explicitly `ephemeral`). Opt-in `EffectfulGraphNodeRunner` persists effect intent before dispatch, records external handles, and reconciles uncertain/accepted effects on `run(resume=True)`. `ArmedCrashProbe` / `InjectedProcessCrash` inject process failure at recovery boundaries. EventLog stays observational; fingerprint refusal remains enforced. Module doctests on `checkpoint_store`, `sqlite_checkpoint_store`, `external_effect`, `graph_executor`, and `MechaHarnessConfig.get_checkpoint_store` show the host wiring pattern.

#### Validation

Kind `transactional_durable_resume_crash_matrix`. Soft expects per crash location: final status ok, dispatch_count exactly 1 after an accepted first dispatch, effect state transitions, and reconciliation on uncertain/accepted resumes. Unit matrix in `tests/test_transactional_durable_resume.py`. Pytest `--doctest-modules` covers the pydoc examples under `src/mechaharness/{checkpoint_store,sqlite_checkpoint_store,external_effect,graph_executor,di}.py`.

#### Footnotes

[^tdr-req]: [Transactional durable graph resume requirements](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/requirements/transactional-durable-resume.md) — DR-01..DR-12 — checkpoint seam, SQLite, effect reconciliation, crash matrix

### `fangore_verification_outcome_gate` — Treat answer generated as distinct from task complete

Fangore's pipeline produces an answer and still needs verification before the task is complete. When verification is required, generating text alone must not count as done; when verification passes, completion can proceed. Complements `fangore_bounded_repair_loop`. See inspiration requirements for verification as part of execution[^insp-verify].

#### Implementation

`OutcomeContract` in `mechaharness.outcome_contract` distinguishes `answer_generated`, `verified`, `complete`, and `failed`. `DefaultVerificationPolicy` selects the strongest sufficient oracle and gates completion through the outcome contract when `require_verification` is set.

#### Validation

Kind `verification_outcome_gate` → `_run_verification_outcome_gate`. Soft expects: answer without verification stays `answer_generated`; verification pass yields `complete`. Unit: `tests/test_inspiration_primitives.py`.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-verify]: [Inspiration requirements (verification)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 5 — verification policy; answer generated ≠ task complete

## Taloneth's stories

### `taloneth_atk_research_reject` — Reject research candidates that fail verified success

A cheap backend fails verified success against a frozen baseline. Research must reject it, keep negative results, and only promote noninferior survivors. Candidates cannot rewrite the evaluator. Related: `taloneth_validator_qualification`.

#### Implementation

`ResearchLab` / `EvalProtocol` run bounded research: inspect → hypothesis → isolated experiment → ATK-style search → frozen evaluation protocol → promote/rollback. Production evaluators stay protected.

Covers: EXP-01, EXP-02, EXP-03, EXP-04.

#### Validation

Kind `atk_research_reject` → `_run_atk_research_reject`. Unit: `tests/test_research.py`.

### `taloneth_cache_layout_experiment` — Measure cache-aware prompt layout as an explicit experiment

Taloneth toggles cache-aware layout on and off. When enabled, stable policy blocks should sit in a stable prefix separate from the dynamic tail; when disabled, everything stays in the dynamic tail with diagnostics.

#### Implementation

`compile_cache_aware_layout` / `CacheLayout` under `CtxFlags.cache_aware_layout` — an independent experiment toggle with prefix identity diagnostics.

Covers: CTX-09.

#### Validation

Kind `cache_layout_experiment` → `_run_cache_layout_experiment`. Unit: `tests/test_context_experiments.py`.

### `taloneth_fixture_judge_batch` — Validate judge question batches without a live model

Taloneth iterates yes/no, choice, and score questions offline. Clean batches validate; missing answers must surface structured errors — including partial failure reporting — without a GPU host.

#### Implementation

Provider-neutral judge schema in `mechaharness.inference.judge` (`Choice`/`Noul`/`Score` questions and signals, `Judgement`, `JudgeErrorItem`, provenance). `FixtureJudgeProvider` + `judge()` validate batches and report per-question errors. Semantics cover closed-world answers, partial failure, and calibration/provenance fields adapters must map.

Covers: JDG-01, JDG-02, JDG-03, JDG-04.

#### Validation

Kind `fixture_judge_batch` → `_run_fixture_judge_batch`. Unit: `tests/test_judge.py`.

### `taloneth_harness_experiment_retire` — Retire scaffolding that loses a with-versus-without experiment

Taloneth treats a prompt scaffold as a hypothesis: keep it only if the with-intervention arm beats the without arm on the primary metric. When the scaffold hurts, it is retired rather than left as fossil control logic. See inspiration requirements for revisable scaffolding and harness hypotheses[^insp-experiment].

#### Implementation

`HarnessExperiment` / `HarnessExperimentRunner` in `mechaharness.harness_experiment` express interventions as hypotheses with expected metrics, compare with/without arms, and list retirement candidates. Integrates with `ResearchLab` for offline evaluation. Trace fields expose experiment id, harness version, and assignment.

#### Validation

Kind `harness_experiment_retire` → `_run_harness_experiment_retire`. Soft expects: treatment worse than control yields `retired` status and a retirement candidate. Related: `taloneth_atk_research_reject`. Unit: `tests/test_inspiration_primitives.py`.

[^insp-experiment]: [Inspiration requirements (harness experiments)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Reqs 1 and 14 — revisable scaffolding; harness changes as testable hypotheses

`ComponentAblationExperiment` and `ablation_delta` in `mechaharness.component_ablation` standardize baseline fingerprint, disabled component IDs, and quality/cost deltas.

### `taloneth_validator_qualification` — Qualify validators before they gate completion

Before a schema validator gates done, known-good, known-bad, and missing fixtures must run — including a weak always-pass mutant that must fail qualification. Judge scores alone cannot complete a task (see `fangore_refund_verdict`).

#### Implementation

`VerificationOracle` / `verify_node` define completion evidence; `qualify_validator` / `validator_qualified` reject always-pass mutants. Judge quality signals remain supplementary to evidence checks.

Covers: VER-01, VER-04.

#### Validation

Kind `validator_qualification` → `_run_validator_qualification`. Unit: `tests/test_graph.py`.
